paragraphs: Friend, here's the verdict on Amaziah: he did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, but not wholeheartedly (2 Chronicles 25:2). He follows the Law of Moses when it comes to the murderers' sons (2 Chronicles 25:4). Then he comes home from a win and sets up the gods of Seir as his own (2 Chronicles 25:14). A half-hearted yes to God is still a half-hearted yes, and it shows up exactly when the pressure and the victory hit.

Now notice the two times God's word reaches Amaziah. A man of God tells him to send Israel's army home, and even after Amaziah asks about the hundred talents he already paid, he hears "The LORD is able to give you much more than this" and sends them home (2 Chronicles 25:7-10). Then a prophet asks why he would seek gods that "could not deliver" their own people from him, and Amaziah says, "Stop!" (2 Chronicles 25:15-16). Friend, he obeyed when it cost him silver, but he told the prophet to stop when the word was about his new gods.

So here's the big idea, baker. God doesn't want the part of us that's convenient, He wants all of it, including the day after the win when nobody's asking. The prophet's last word is a hard one: God "has determined to destroy" Amaziah because he did this and did not heed the advice (2 Chronicles 25:16). Ask yourself where you've been giving God a yes with a catch, then bring Him the whole batch, and I'll keep the ovens warm for you.
